title: Comparison Between Two Methodologies of Sample Preservation for RNA Extraction in Naturally Delivered Ovine Placenta
content: Placental samples for RNA extraction are collected via invasive methods (post-mortem or surgically) in small ruminants. An alternative could be using delivered placentas, but the feasibility of obtaining high-quality RNA from this tissue has not been determined. We aimed to evaluate the possibility of extracting RNA from naturally delivered ovine placenta, comparing two preservation methods. Twenty-seven single-pregnant sheep were monitored 24/7 from gestational day 140 to parturition. Tissue was collected immediately after placental delivery, preserved using Snap Frozen (SF, n=27) and RNAlater® (LTR, n=27) techniques, and processed for RNA extraction using a commercial kit. RNA concentration (ng/uL), A260/280, and RNA Quality Number (RQN) were measured. Concentration was higher (p < 0.001) in LTR (70.39 ± 6.3) than in SF (49.77 ± 10.5), A260/280 was higher (p = 0.045) in SF (2.06 ± 0.01) than in LTR (2.03 ± 0.01), and RQN was higher (p < 0.0001) in SF (6.81 ± 0.24) than LTR (2.84 ± 0.24) samples. The timing of placental delivery did not affect the evaluated indicators. Our results indicate that extracting high-quality RNA from delivered placenta preserved via snap frozen technique is possible, supporting a method that aligns with the refinement principle of animals used in research.
